record.paper_title: Subsums of Null Sequences: A Survey and Open Questions
record.original_question: Let α_i and λ_i be null sequences with α_i → 0 and λ_i → 0, and for each i let K_i be the middle-α_i Cantor set whose first construction interval is [0, λ_i]. If S is the associated sumset and R_z is the tail set, under what conditions on R_z and on the parameters α_i is S a finite interval or a finite union of intervals?

evidence.quote:

intervals or a union of finite intervals?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each i ∈ ℕ, let α_i ∈ (0,1) and λ_i > 0 be parameters with α_i → 0 and λ_i → 0 as i → ∞. The "middle-α_i Cantor set with initial interval [0, λ_i]" is the compact set K_i ⊂ [0, λ_i] obtained by the following iterated procedure: start with the closed interval [0, λ_i]; at each step, from every closed interval J of the current collection remove the open middle subinterval of length α_i · |J|, leaving two closed subintervals of length (1−α_i)|J|/2 each; K_i is the intersection of the nested unions thus obtained.

For a fixed positive integer z, define the "tail set"
   R_z = { ∑_{i>z} x_i : x_i ∈ K_i for each i > z },
i.e. the set of all sums of selections of one point from each K_i for i > z (assumed convergent). Define the associated sumset
   S = K_1 + K_2 + ⋯ + K_z + R_z = { y_1 + ⋯ + y_z + r : y_i ∈ K_i, r ∈ R_z }.

Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the tail set R_z and on the sequence of parameters (α_i)_{i ∈ ℕ} under which S is a (nondegenerate) closed interval, and more generally under which S is a finite union of closed intervals.
artifact.category_tag: Subsums of null sequences and Cantor sumsets
artifact.status_search_result: The question concerns when sums involving middle-α Cantor sets with vanishing parameters yield intervals or finite unions of intervals. While general structural results are known (e.g., subsum sets of absolutely summable null sequences are finite unions of intervals, Cantor sets, or Cantorvals; sums of central Cantor sets fall into the same trichotomy), no complete characterization in terms of the tail set R_z together with the parameters α_i appears in the literature located. Related recent work (e.g., conditions for difference sets of central Cantor sets to be Cantorvals, 2023) addresses adjacent but not identical questions. The problem appears to be open.

status_evidence.title: Cantorvals and Subsum Sets of Null Sequences
status_evidence.snippet: Subsum set of an absolutely summable sequence is a finite union of compact intervals, a Cantor set, or a symmetric Cantorval.
status_evidence.claim: General trichotomy is known but parameter-level characterization for middle-α Cantor sumsets is not given.

status_evidence.title: Conditions for the Difference Set of a Central Cantor Set to be a Cantorval
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2023) work studies when difference sets of central Cantor sets become Cantorvals.
status_evidence.claim: Adjacent question remains under active study, suggesting the interval-classification version is still open.

status_evidence.title: A Technique of Studying Sums of Central Cantor Sets
status_evidence.snippet: Sums of central Cantor sets are Cantor sets, finite unions of closed intervals, or Cantorvals.
status_evidence.claim: Trichotomy known; sharp conditions in the null-sequence regime are not provided.
